title: The Save File That Wasn't Mine
style: moody stylized digital illustration, cinematic lighting, muted colors with one neon accent, no text in the image

characters.Mia: a tired 20-something gamer with messy black hair and an oversized green hoodie

scenes.narration: At 3 a.m., Mia found a save file on her old console that she never created.
scenes.image_prompt: a dim bedroom, an old console glowing in the dark, a menu showing one unfamiliar save slot

scenes.narration: Slot one. Playtime: 412 hours. Last played: tomorrow.
scenes.image_prompt: extreme close-up of a game menu screen, glitching numbers, neon cyan accent

scenes.narration: She told herself it was a bug. Consoles do that. Dates break. Memory corrupts. She loaded it anyway, because that is what everyone does.
scenes.image_prompt: Mia leaning toward a TV, controller in hand, face lit blue by the screen

scenes.narration: The game opened in her bedroom. Her actual bedroom. Same poster, same cracked window. The character standing in it wore her hoodie.
scenes.image_prompt: a video game render of a realistic bedroom with a character in a green hoodie standing with their back turned

scenes.narration: Then the character turned around, looked straight out of the screen, and typed one line into the chat. Don't save over this.
scenes.image_prompt: a character in a green hoodie facing the viewer, a chat box with a short line of text implied, eerie glow

scenes.narration: Mia did what she always does. She pressed save.
scenes.image_prompt: a lone finger above a glowing save button, the room around it dark and silent
